components.heading: Linux Lab 04: Kernel source walkthrough, pinned to v6.6

payload.title: Kernel source walkthrough, pinned to v6.6
payload.summary: Navigate two authored Linux v6.6 source-reading routes for TCP ingress and egress, then cross the TCP_INFO UAPI boundary without copying or executing kernel code.

prerequisites: Comfort reading C signatures, return contracts, and failure paths
Awareness that sk_buff, socket state, route callbacks, hooks, and UAPI copies cross different ownership boundaries
Understanding that authored reading edges can be direct calls, callbacks, continuations, or observation boundaries
outcomes: Follow ingress from receive core through IPv4 local delivery to TCP acknowledgement processing
Follow egress from sock_sendmsg through TCP write queues, IPv4 output, and device queueing
Compare tcp_get_info with struct tcp_info and explain option-length handling

payload.exercise: Complete the static C index and directed-edge validator in exercise.c without downloading source or adding generated files. Keep data static and immutable so calls require no allocation or global mutation.
payload.reference: The generated walkthrough data defines the exact ingress and egress ID arrays, symbol metadata, source URLs, and UAPI bridge records used by the reference implementation.
checks: Unique IDs and exact ingress and egress sequences are required
Unknown, reversed, skipped, and non-adjacent teaching edges are rejected
URLs are HTTPS links pinned to /v6.6/ and capacity queries produce no partial URL
The CLI handles list, route, symbol lookup, unknown options, unknown keys, and extra arguments deterministically

allowed: Pinned links to Linux v6.6 source for study and provenance
Independently authored navigation metadata, descriptions, validators, and CLI output
Unprivileged offline source navigation and option-boundary reasoning
excluded: Copying Linux kernel function bodies, comment blocks, tables, source snapshots, or generated files into this repository
Network access, module loading, tracing, probing, privileged operation, or kernel modification
Treating the validator as a call-graph analyzer or modeling every ingress or egress branch, UDP, IPv6, forwarding, raw sockets, XDP, offload, retransmission details, or lock ordering
